phillip_island.surface: Hot-mix asphalt. Abrasive when green; high grip once rubbered in. Coastal salt and wind can polish the line between sessions.
phillip_island.weatherUsual: Exposed Bass Strait circuit. Cool, windy, and changeable — a sea breeze on the main straight is common. Mornings can be cold even in summer.

asbkRecords.source: Computime motorcycle lap records, Jan 2026 (international Superbike)

smp_gardner.surface: Permanent asphalt GP circuit. Grip builds with rubber; night meetings under lights change how the surface looks more than how it feels.
smp_gardner.weatherUsual: Western Sydney. Hot and still in summer; cool, damp mornings in winter. Thunderstorms can sweep through in the afternoon.

asbkRecords.source: Computime motorcycle lap records, Jan 2026 (Gardner GP)

smp_brabham.surface: Same complex as Gardner with the eastern Brabham extension. Extra kerbs and a longer lap — treat the added loop as a separate memory.
smp_brabham.weatherUsual: Western Sydney. Hot and still in summer; cool, damp mornings in winter.

smp_druitt.surface: Shorter western loop of Sydney Motorsport Park. Same asphalt family as Gardner; fewer corners, same pit straight.
smp_druitt.weatherUsual: Western Sydney. Hot and still in summer; cool, damp mornings in winter.

queensland_raceway.surface: Smooth National Circuit asphalt. Relatively flat and consistent; grip is high when rubbered in, slippery if dusty or green.
queensland_raceway.weatherUsual: Ipswich. Warm to hot, with summer storms. Winter mornings can be foggy; the track often dries quickly.

asbkRecords.source: ASBK.com.au race-one report, Queensland Raceway finale (Computime Jan 2026 still listed Josh Waters 1:07.265)

the_bend_international.surface: Wide modern asphalt with generous run-off. High-grip when rubbered; dusty off-line after mixed car/bike days.
the_bend_international.weatherUsual: Tailem Bend, SA. Dry and windy is typical. Summer heat is harsh; winter days are cool and clear more often than wet.

asbkRecords.source: Computime motorcycle lap records, after 2025 ASBK (International Circuit)

the_bend_gt.surface: Longest Australian bitumen layout — International plus the GT extension. Same modern asphalt; more elevation feel over the extra loop than the bake records.
the_bend_gt.weatherUsual: Tailem Bend, SA. Dry and windy is typical. Plan for heat and wind rather than rain.

wakefield_park.surface: One Raceway (formerly Wakefield Park). Compact, bumpy in places, with a short lap that rewards a tidy line.
wakefield_park.weatherUsual: Southern Tablelands. Cooler than the coast; frost or fog is possible in winter. Wind across the hill is common.

asbkRecords.source: Computime One Raceway sheet (current layout after resurface). ASBK.com.au spectator notes match.

morgan_park.surface: Layout K asphalt. Mix of slow hairpins and a decent back straight; grip is good when rubbered, greasy when damp under trees.
morgan_park.weatherUsual: Warwick, QLD. Warm inland climate. Summer storms; winter mornings can be cold in the valleys.

hidden_valley.surface: Smooth tropical asphalt. High grip in the dry; monsoon rain makes it very slippery until it dries.
hidden_valley.weatherUsual: Darwin. Dry season is hot and stable; build-up and wet season bring humidity, storms, and standing water.

asbkRecords.source: Computime Hidden Valley sheet, current at June 2022

winton.surface: National Circuit asphalt with a few bumps. Short, technical, and often dusty off-line.
winton.weatherUsual: North-east Victoria. Hot summers, cold winters. Fog and frost are common early; the afternoon can be much warmer.

sandown.surface: Traditional suburban asphalt with a long start/finish straight. Can be bumpier than newer circuits.
sandown.weatherUsual: Melbourne. Four seasons in a day — take a wet option seriously even if the morning is clear.

mallala.surface: Open, relatively flat asphalt. Dusty off-line; the line rubbers in during a meeting.
mallala.weatherUsual: North of Adelaide. Dry, windy, and exposed. Summer heat and wind are the usual story; rain is less common than heat.

asbkRecords.source: Computime Mallala sheet (updated May 2016; last ASBK-era record on file)

wanneroo.surface: Wanneroo Raceway asphalt. Short, flowing, and well used; grip is usually good on the line.
wanneroo.weatherUsual: Perth. Hot and dry in summer; cool, sometimes wet winters. Sea breeze can arrive in the afternoon.

asbkRecords.source: Computime Barbagallo sheet (updated Jun 2016). Pre-dates the 2019 motorcycle chicane.

broadford.surface: State Motorcycle Complex road-race loop. Tight, technical asphalt with limited run-off in places.
broadford.weatherUsual: Central Victoria. Cooler than Melbourne; fog and damp trees in winter, warm and dry in summer.

asbkRecords.source: Computime Broadford (Reg Hunt Park) sheet, Jan 2026 — state/club, not an ASBK round

mac_park.surface: Mount Gambier Mac Park asphalt. Short club circuit; grip varies with how recently it has been used.
mac_park.weatherUsual: South-east SA. Cooler and more changeable than Adelaide. Wind and passing showers are common.

asbkRecords.source: Computime Mac Park sheet, Jan 2026 — outright superbike, not an ASBK round

calder_park.surface: Thunderdome / road-course asphalt. Club-level surface; dusty if the meeting is quiet.
calder_park.weatherUsual: North-west of Melbourne. Hot and dry in summer; similar changeable pattern to the rest of Melbourne in winter.

baskerville.surface: Compact Tasmanian asphalt. Bumpy in places; grip is decent on the line, greasy in the trees when damp.
baskerville.weatherUsual: Hobart hinterland. Cooler year-round. Wet and cold is the default planning assumption.

lakeside.surface: Old-school asphalt around the lake. Bumpy, technical, and unforgiving off-line.
lakeside.weatherUsual: North of Brisbane. Warm and humid. Summer storms; the lake can add mist on cool mornings.
